V10 and v13 keep the KJV's sons of Belial, explained as (worthless men).

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things, that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by (close to) the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

And Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying: Give me your vineyard, so that I may have it for a garden of herbs (vegetables), because it is near to my house. And I will give you for it a better vineyard than it. Or, if it seem good to you, I will give you the worth of it in money.
And Naboth said to Ahab: The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance (family land) of my fathers to you.

And Ahab came into his house heavy (sad) and displeased because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him. For Naboth had said: I will not give you the inheritance (family land) of my fathers. And Ahab laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and would eat no bread.
But Jezebel his wife came to him, and said to him: Why is your spirit so sad, that you eat no bread?

And Ahab said to her: Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite, and said to him: Give me your vineyard for money. Or else, if it please you, I will give you another vineyard for it. And he answered: I will not give you my vineyard.

And Jezebel his wife said to him: Do you now govern (rule) the kingdom of Israel? Arise (get up), and eat bread, and let your heart be merry (happy). I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.

So Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name, and sealed them with his seal (stamp), and sent the letters to the elders and to the nobles (important men) that were in Naboth's city, dwelling (living) with Naboth.
And she wrote in the letters, saying: Proclaim a fast (announce a day of no eating), and set Naboth on high (in a high seat) among the people.

And set 2 men, sons of Belial (worthless men), before him, to bear witness against him, saying: You did blaspheme (speak against) God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him, so that he may die.

And the men of his city, even the elders and the nobles (important men) who were the inhabitants (people) in his city, did as Jezebel had sent to them, and as it was written in the letters which she had sent to them.
They proclaimed a fast (announced a day of no eating), and set Naboth on high (in a high seat) among the people.

And there came in 2 men, children of Belial (worthless men), and sat before him. And the men of Belial (worthless men) witnessed against him, even against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying: Naboth did blaspheme (speak against) God and the king. Then they carried him forth (out) out of the city, and stoned him with stones, so that he died.
Then they sent to Jezebel, saying: Naboth is stoned, and is dead.

And it came to pass, when Jezebel heard that Naboth was stoned, and was dead, that Jezebel said to Ahab: Arise (get up), take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for money. For Naboth is not alive, but dead.
And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab rose up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
And the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite (from Tishbe), saying:
Arise (get up), go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, which is in Samaria. Look, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he is gone down to possess (take) it.

And you shall speak to him, saying: This is what the LORD says: Have you killed, and also taken possession? And you shall speak to him, saying: This is what the LORD says: In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick your blood, even yours.
And Ahab said to Elijah: Have you found me, O my enemy? And Elijah answered: I have found you, because you have sold yourself to work evil in the sight of the LORD.

Look, I will bring evil upon you, and will take away your posterity (family line), and will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall (every male), and him that is shut up and left in Israel.

And I will make your house (family) like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, for the provocation (anger) with which you have provoked Me to anger, and made Israel to sin.
And of Jezebel also the LORD spoke, saying: The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.
Him that dies of Ahab's family in the city the dogs shall eat. And him that dies in the field shall the fowls (birds) of the air eat.
But there was none like Ahab, which did sell himself to work wickedness in the sight of the LORD, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.
And Ahab did very abominably (hatefully) in following idols, according to all things as did the Amorites, whom the LORD cast out before the children of Israel.

And it came to pass, when Ahab heard those words, that he rent (tore) his clothes, and put sackcloth (rough cloth worn in sorrow) upon his flesh (body), and fasted (did not eat), and lay in sackcloth, and went softly (walked humbly).
And the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite (from Tishbe), saying:
Do you see how Ahab humbles himself before Me? Because he humbles himself before Me, I will not bring the evil in his days. But in his son's days will I bring the evil upon his house (family).

verses.text: And look, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the LORD to Bethel. And Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense (sweet-smelling spice).

And the man of God cried against the altar in the word of the LORD, and said: O altar, altar, this is what the LORD says: Look, a child shall be born to the house (family) of David, Josiah by name. And upon you shall he offer the priests of the high places (idol altars) that burn incense (sweet-smelling spice) upon you, and men's bones shall be burnt upon you.
And he gave a sign the same day, saying: This is the sign which the LORD has spoken: Look, the altar shall be rent (split), and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.

And it came to pass, when king Jeroboam heard the saying of the man of God, which had cried against the altar in Bethel, that he put forth (out) his hand from the altar, saying: Lay hold on (grab) him. And his hand, which he put forth (out) against him, dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.
The altar also was rent (split), and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

And the king answered and said to the man of God: Intreat (pray to) now the face of the LORD your God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored (healed) to me again. And the man of God besought (begged) the LORD, and the king's hand was restored (healed) to him again, and became as it was before.
And the king said to the man of God: Come home with me, and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.
And the man of God said to the king: If you will give me half your house, I will not go in with you, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place.
For so was it charged (commanded) me by the word of the LORD, saying: Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that you came.
So the man of God went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Bethel.

Now there dwelt (lived) an old prophet in Bethel. And his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. The words which he had spoken to the king, them they told also to their father.
And their father said to them: What way did he go? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.
And the old prophet said to his sons: Saddle me the ass (donkey). So they saddled him the ass (donkey). And he rode on it,
And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak. And the old prophet said to him: Are you the man of God that came from Judah? And he said: I am.
Then the old prophet said to him: Come home with me, and eat bread.
And the man of God said: I may not return with you, nor go in with you. Neither will I eat bread nor drink water with you in this place.
For it was said to me by the word of the LORD: You shall eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that you came.

The old prophet said to him: I am a prophet also as you are. And an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying: Bring him back with you into your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water. But the old prophet lied to him.
So the man of God went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.
And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the LORD came to the prophet that brought him back.

And he cried to the man of God that came from Judah, saying: This is what the LORD says: Forasmuch as (because) you have disobeyed the mouth of the LORD, and have not kept the commandment which the LORD your God commanded you,

But came back, and have eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of which the LORD did say to you: Eat no bread, and drink no water, your carcase (dead body) shall not come to the sepulchre (tomb) of your fathers.
And it came to pass, after the man of God had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that the old prophet saddled for him the ass (donkey), that is, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

And when the man of God was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew (killed) him. And his carcase (dead body) was cast (thrown) in the way, and the ass (donkey) stood by it. The lion also stood by the carcase (dead body).

And look, men passed by, and saw the carcase (dead body) cast (thrown) in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase (dead body). And they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt (lived).

And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard of it, he said: It is the man of God, who was disobedient to the word of the LORD. Therefore the LORD has delivered (handed) him to the lion, which has torn him, and slain (killed) him, according to the word of the LORD, which He spoke to him.
And the old prophet spoke to his sons, saying: Saddle me the ass (donkey). And they saddled him.

And he went and found the carcase (dead body) cast (thrown) in the way, and the ass (donkey) and the lion standing by the carcase (dead body). The lion had not eaten the carcase (dead body), nor torn the ass (donkey).
And the prophet took up the carcase (dead body) of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass (donkey), and brought it back. And the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.
And he laid his carcase (dead body) in his own grave. And they mourned over him, saying: Alas (oh, how sad), my brother!
And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spoke to his sons, saying: When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre (tomb) in which the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.

For the saying which he cried by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places (idol altars) which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass (happen).

After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places (idol altars). Whoever would, he consecrated (set apart) him, and he became one of the priests of the high places.
And this thing became sin to the house (family) of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the face of the earth.

17.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Verses 17-24 (Elijah raising the widow's son) were missing and have been restored.

verses.text: And Elijah the Tishbite (from Tishbe), who was of the inhabitants (people) of Gilead, said to Ahab: As the LORD God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.
And the word of the LORD came to Elijah, saying:
Get away from here, and turn eastward, and hide yourself by the brook (stream) Cherith, that is before the Jordan.
And it shall be, that you shall drink of the brook (stream). And I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.
So Elijah went and did according to the word of the LORD. For he went and dwelt (lived) by the brook (stream) Cherith, that is before the Jordan.
And the ravens brought him bread and flesh (meat) in the morning, and bread and flesh (meat) in the evening. And he drank of the brook (stream).
And it came to pass after a while, that the brook (stream) dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
And the word of the LORD came to Elijah, saying:
Arise (get up), go to Zarephath, which belongs to Zidon, and dwell (live) there. Look, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain (feed) you.

So Elijah arose (got up) and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, look, the widow woman was there gathering sticks. And he called to her, and said: Fetch (bring) me, I pray you (please), a little water in a vessel (cup), so that I may drink.
And as she was going to fetch (get) it, he called to her, and said: Bring me, I pray you (please), a morsel (piece) of bread in your hand.

And she said: As the LORD your God lives, I have not a cake (loaf), but an handful of meal (flour) in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse (small jar). And look, I am gathering 2 sticks, so that I may go in and dress (cook) it for me and my son, so that we may eat it, and die.
And Elijah said to her: Fear not. Go and do as you have said. But make me of it a little cake (loaf) first, and bring it to me, and after that make for you and for your son.

For this is what the LORD God of Israel says: The barrel of meal (flour) shall not waste (run out), neither shall the cruse (small jar) of oil fail (run dry), until the day that the LORD sends rain upon the earth.
And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah. And she, and he, and her house (family), did eat many days.
And the barrel of meal (flour) wasted (ran out) not, neither did the cruse (small jar) of oil fail (run dry), according to the word of the LORD, which He spoke by Elijah.
And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress (owner) of the house, fell sick. And his sickness was so sore (bad), that there was no breath left in him.
And she said to Elijah: What have I to do with you, O man of God? Are you come to me to call my sin to remembrance (to remind God of my sin), and to slay (kill) my son?
And Elijah said to her: Give me your son. And he took him out of her bosom (arms), and carried him up into a loft (upstairs room), where he abode (stayed), and laid him upon his own bed.
And Elijah cried to the LORD, and said: O LORD my God, have You also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn (stay), by slaying (killing) her son?
And Elijah stretched himself upon the child 3 times, and cried to the LORD, and said: O LORD my God, I pray You, let this child's soul come into him again.
And the LORD heard the voice of Elijah. And the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived (came back to life).
And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber (room) into the house, and delivered (gave) him to his mother. And Elijah said: See, your son lives.
And the woman said to Elijah: Now by this I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth.

18.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that added things the KJV does not say, e.g. 'maybe he stepped out for a moment' in v27), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V21 keeps the KJV's How long halt ye between two opinions? V39 keeps The LORD, He is the God.

verses.text: And it came to pass after many days, that the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the 3rd year, saying: Go, show yourself to Ahab. And I will send rain upon the earth.
And Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. And there was a sore (terrible) famine (no food) in Samaria.
And Ahab called Obadiah, which was the governor (manager) of his house. (Now Obadiah feared the LORD greatly.
For it was so, when Jezebel cut off (killed) the prophets of the LORD, that Obadiah took 100 prophets, and hid them by 50 in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)

And Ahab said to Obadiah: Go into the land, to all fountains (springs) of water, and to all brooks (streams). Peradventure (maybe) we may find grass to save the horses and mules alive, so that we lose not all the beasts (animals).
So they divided the land between them to pass throughout it. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
And as Obadiah was in the way, look, Elijah met him. And Obadiah knew him, and fell on his face, and said: Are you my lord Elijah?
And Elijah answered him: I am. Go, tell your lord: Look, Elijah is here.
And Obadiah said: What have I sinned, that you would deliver (hand) your servant into the hand of Ahab, to slay (kill) me?

As the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom, where my lord has not sent to seek (look for) you. And when they said: He is not there, he took an oath (made them promise) of the kingdom and nation, that they found you not.
And now you say: Go, tell your lord: Look, Elijah is here.

And it shall come to pass, as soon as I am gone from you, that the Spirit of the LORD shall carry you where I know not. And so when I come and tell Ahab, and he cannot find you, he shall slay (kill) me. But I your servant fear the LORD from my youth.
Was it not told my lord what I did when Jezebel slew (killed) the prophets of the LORD, how I hid 100 men of the LORD's prophets by 50 in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
And now you say: Go, tell your lord: Look, Elijah is here. And he shall slay (kill) me.
And Elijah said: As the LORD of hosts (armies) lives, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself to him to day (today).
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and told him. And Ahab went to meet Elijah.
And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said to him: Are you he that troubles Israel?

And Elijah answered: I have not troubled Israel. But you, and your father's house (family), have, in that you have forsaken (left) the commandments of the LORD, and you have followed Baalim (the Baal idols).
Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel to mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal 450, and the prophets of the groves (Asherah idols) 400, which eat at Jezebel's table.
So Ahab sent to all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together to mount Carmel.

And Elijah came to all the people, and said: How long halt you between two opinions (go back and forth between two choices)? If the LORD be God, follow Him. But if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
Then Elijah said to the people: I, even I only, remain a prophet of the LORD. But Baal's prophets are 450 men.

Let them therefore give us 2 bullocks (young bulls). And let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under. And I will dress (prepare) the other bullock, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under.
And call on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the LORD. And the God that answers by fire, let Him be God. And all the people answered and said: It is well spoken.
And Elijah said to the prophets of Baal: Choose one bullock (young bull) for yourselves, and dress (prepare) it first, for you are many. And call on the name of your gods, but put no fire under.

And they took the bullock (young bull) which was given them, and they dressed (prepared) it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying: O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped upon the altar which was made.

And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked (made fun of) them, and said: Cry aloud, for he is a god. Either he is talking, or he is pursuing (busy chasing something), or he is in a journey, or peradventure (maybe) he sleeps, and must be awaked.
And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner (custom) with knives and lancets (spears), till the blood gushed out upon them.

And it came to pass, when midday was past, and they prophesied (acted like prophets) until the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded (paid attention).
And Elijah said to all the people: Come near to me. And all the people came near to him. And Elijah repaired the altar of the LORD that was broken down.
And Elijah took 12 stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD came, saying: Israel shall be your name.
And with the stones Elijah built an altar in the name of the LORD. And he made a trench (ditch) around the altar, as great as would contain (hold) 2 measures of seed.
And Elijah put the wood in order, and cut the bullock (young bull) in pieces, and laid it on the wood, and said: Fill 4 barrels with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice, and on the wood.
And Elijah said: Do it the 2nd time. And they did it the 2nd time. And he said: Do it the 3rd time. And they did it the 3rd time.
And the water ran round about the altar. And Elijah filled the trench (ditch) also with water.

And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said: LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that You are God in Israel, and that I am Your servant, and that I have done all these things at Your word.
Hear me, O LORD, hear me, so that this people may know that You are the LORD God, and that You have turned their heart back again.
Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed (burned up) the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench (ditch).
And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces. And they said: The LORD, He is the God. The LORD, He is the God.
And Elijah said to them: Take the prophets of Baal. Let not one of them escape. And they took them. And Elijah brought them down to the brook (stream) Kishon, and slew (killed) them there.
And Elijah said to Ahab: Get up, eat and drink. For there is a sound of abundance (a lot) of rain.
So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel. And he cast (threw) himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees,
And said to his servant: Go up now, look toward the sea. And the servant went up, and looked, and said: There is nothing. And Elijah said: Go again 7 times.

And it came to pass at the 7th time, that the servant said: Look, there arises a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand. And Elijah said: Go up, say to Ahab: Prepare your chariot, and get down, so that the rain stop you not.
And it came to pass in the mean while (meantime), that the heaven was black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel.
And the hand of the LORD was on Elijah. And he girded up his loins (tucked his robe into his belt), and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

19.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V12 keeps the KJV's still small voice. V10 and v14 write covenant as agreement, as elsewhere on the site.

verses.text: And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal (also) how he had slain (killed) all the prophets with the sword.
Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying: So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not your life as the life of one of them by to morrow (tomorrow) about this time.
And when Elijah saw that, he arose (got up), and went for his life, and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.

But Elijah himself went a day's journey into the wilderness (desert), and came and sat down under a juniper tree. And he requested (asked) for himself that he might die, and said: It is enough. Now, O LORD, take away my life. For I am not better than my fathers.
And as Elijah lay and slept under a juniper tree, look, then an angel touched him, and said to him: Arise (get up) and eat.
And Elijah looked, and look, there was a cake (loaf) baken (baked) on the coals, and a cruse (small jar) of water at his head. And he did eat and drink, and laid him down again.
And the angel of the LORD came again the 2nd time, and touched him, and said: Arise (get up) and eat, because the journey is too great for you.
And Elijah arose (got up), and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat (food) 40 days and 40 nights to Horeb the mount of God.
And Elijah came there to a cave, and lodged (stayed) there. And look, the word of the LORD came to him, and the LORD said to him: What are you doing here, Elijah?

And Elijah said: I have been very jealous (zealous) for the LORD God of hosts (armies). For the children of Israel have forsaken (left) Your agreement, thrown down Your altars, and slain (killed) Your prophets with the sword. And I, even I only, am left. And they seek (look for) my life, to take it away.

And the LORD said: Go forth (out), and stand upon the mount before the LORD. And look, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent (tore) the mountains, and brake (broke) in pieces the rocks before the LORD. But the LORD was not in the wind. And after the wind an earthquake. But the LORD was not in the earthquake.
And after the earthquake a fire. But the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire a still small voice (a quiet, gentle whisper).

And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle (cloak), and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave. And look, there came a voice to him, and said: What are you doing here, Elijah?

And Elijah said: I have been very jealous (zealous) for the LORD God of hosts (armies), because the children of Israel have forsaken (left) Your agreement, thrown down Your altars, and slain (killed) Your prophets with the sword. And I, even I only, am left. And they seek (look for) my life, to take it away.
And the LORD said to Elijah: Go, return on your way to the wilderness (desert) of Damascus. And when you come, anoint (pour oil on) Hazael to be king over Syria.
And Jehu the son of Nimshi you shall anoint (pour oil on) to be king over Israel. And Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abelmeholah you shall anoint (pour oil on) to be prophet in your room (place).
And it shall come to pass, that him that escapes the sword of Hazael shall Jehu slay (kill). And him that escapes from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha slay (kill).
Yet I have left Me 7,000 in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth which has not kissed him.

So Elijah departed (went) from there, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with 12 yoke (pairs) of oxen before him, and he with the 12th. And Elijah passed by him, and cast (threw) his mantle (cloak) upon him.

And Elisha left the oxen, and ran after Elijah, and said: Let me, I pray you (please), kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you. And Elijah said to him: Go back again. For what have I done to you?

And Elisha returned back from him, and took a yoke (pair) of oxen, and slew (killed) them, and boiled their flesh (meat) with the instruments (wooden tools) of the oxen, and gave to the people, and they did eat. Then he arose (got up), and went after Elijah, and ministered (served) to him.
